title: Anatomical homeostasis uses large-scale feedback loops that reduce error from a target

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anatomical homeostasis uses large-scale feedback loops that reduce error from a target

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Morphogenetic problem-solving cases indicate that anatomical development is not entirely open-loop: large-scale feedback loops measure distance from a target anatomical state and execute diverse molecular steps to reduce the error, and such networks can store setpoints that are complex data structures rather than simple scalars.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › The Collective Intelligence of Cell Groups › The Competencies of Anatomical Homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These examples indicate that these processes are not entirely open‐loop: large‐scale feedback loops exist that measure distance from a given target state and execute diverse molecular steps to implement those goals (reduce error).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “The Collective Intelligence of Cell Groups › The Competencies of Anatomical Homeostasis”. Scope: Regulative development and regeneration in animals (e.g. the cases in the paper's Table 1)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Feedback models generate measurable recovery dynamics, and public imaging can test selected cases. Current data do not span the diverse systems claimed or cleanly distinguish explicit target comparison from emergent attractor dynamics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit open-loop and feedback-control models to time-resolved anatomical recovery after graded perturbations, testing whether correction magnitude depends on deviation from a stable morphology and ceases near the target. Superior out-of-sample feedback predictions support anatomical error reduction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stable attractors can mimic explicit error measurement.

The physical storage of complex setpoints is not directly observed.

Most perturbation studies lack dense time series.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.45
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Classic regulative experiments are published measurements of recovery after displacement, so the open-loop versus feedback contrast can be examined for particular organs. Those records are not a harmonized dataset, and they do not encode the molecular steps or show that the stored target is a complex data structure. The feedback idea is partly testable; the data-structure clause is not resolved by what is public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a defined anatomical perturbation, test whether the system reduces an error relative to a species-typical target by alternative molecular routes, or instead follows a fixed sequence that does not depend on the remaining error. Return toward the target by more than one route favors closed-loop homeostasis; a single obligatory sequence favors open-loop development.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nothing currently measures whether a setpoint is a complex data structure rather than a scalar or a gradient.

Error relative to a target can be redescribed as late-acting induction without a stored setpoint.

Perturbation-recovery series are scattered through the embryological literature and are not one dataset.

data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.65
